name: Dekeling Hotel
price_band: ₹2,000–4,000 a room (indicative, higher in peak weeks)
summary: A Tibetan family-run hotel on Gandhi Road, a four- or five-minute walk below Chowrasta. About 28 rooms over several floors, wood-panelled and warm, with the owners usually on site. Long a favourite of budget travellers who want a central bed without a chain-hotel bill.
body: Dekeling sits on Gandhi Road at Clubside, opposite the car park, so you can step out of a shared jeep from Siliguri and be at the reception in minutes. The hotel is owned by the Dekeva family, Tibetan Darjeeling people, and that shows in the details: carpets, painted woodwork, butter tea if you ask, and a family that treats the place as home rather than a franchise. It is classed as a budget hotel with two-star comforts.

Rooms vary a lot by floor and outlook. The upper rooms are quieter and some catch a slice of the mountains; lower rooms face the road. Winter nights drop close to freezing, so ask about heaters and hot water when you book. Being central, you can walk to the Mall, Glenary's, the toy train station and the Chowk Bazaar jeep stands without paying for a taxi, which is real money saved over a three-night stay.
why: Four or five minutes on foot from Chowrasta and the Mall
Run by the same Tibetan family for decades, owners usually present
Close to the Clubside jeep stops, so no taxi on arrival

faqs.q: How far is Dekeling Hotel from the Mall and Chowrasta?
faqs.a: About four to five minutes on foot, uphill. The hotel is on Gandhi Road at Clubside, opposite the car park, so it is also one of the easier central hotels to reach with luggage. Most shared jeeps from Siliguri stop within a short walk, and the railway station is about ten minutes downhill along Hill Cart Road.

faqs.q: Is Dekeling a good choice in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, if you ask for a room with a heater and confirm hot-water hours when you book. Darjeeling nights in December and January fall to about 2 °C, and old hill buildings hold the cold. Upper-floor rooms are usually warmer and quieter. Pack a warm layer for evenings inside, as most hill hotels have no central heating.

faqs.q: Can families stay at Dekeling Hotel?
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel has rooms of different sizes, and its central position suits families who do not want long walks uphill at the end of the day. Ask for a larger room or two connecting rooms early in peak periods such as May, June, October and the Durga Puja and Diwali holidays, when central Darjeeling fills up fast.

name: Darjeeling Tourist Lodge (Meghbalika)
summary: The state-run tourist lodge on Bhanu Sarani, five or six minutes from Chowrasta, now renamed Meghbalika. A main building with about 15 rooms plus economy rooms in an annexe, a garden, a terrace and a restaurant. Plain, central and dependable.
body: For decades the Darjeeling Tourist Lodge was the default address for Bengali families on a hill holiday, and it still works the same way: a solid government building on the steep stretch of Bhanu Sarani, a short climb from Chowrasta, with simple rooms and a dining hall. It has been renamed Meghbalika, but most taxi drivers still know it by the old name. Its address puts you above the worst of the market traffic yet close enough to walk to the Mall, Glenary's and the Chowrasta benches for sunrise.

Expect government-lodge comfort rather than boutique touches: clean linen, basic furniture, a heater on request in winter, and staff who have seen every kind of traveller. The garden and terrace are pleasant on a clear morning. Book well ahead for October, the Puja holidays and May–June. Tariffs, booking channels and the lodge's management have changed over the years, so check current status before you travel. Being a state property, it is also one of the few places in central Darjeeling where the price in peak week is close to the price in the off season.
why: Government-run, with predictable rooms and no surprise extras
Five or six minutes from Chowrasta on Bhanu Sarani
Garden, terrace and an in-house restaurant

faqs.q: Is the Darjeeling Tourist Lodge the same as Meghbalika?
faqs.a: Yes. The state-run Darjeeling Tourist Lodge on Bhanu Sarani has been renamed Meghbalika Tourism Property. Many drivers and older guidebooks still use the old name. It keeps its main building of about 15 rooms and economy rooms in an annexe. Check current booking channels and tariffs before you travel, as these have changed over time.

faqs.q: How steep is the walk to the Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Short but steep. The lodge sits on a sloping part of Bhanu Sarani, five or six minutes from Chowrasta. Most people manage it easily, but older travellers and anyone with heavy bags may prefer a taxi to the nearest drop point. In return you are above much of the traffic noise of the lower town.

faqs.q: Does the lodge serve meals?
faqs.a: Yes, there is a restaurant on site, which is useful on cold or rainy evenings when you do not want to walk back up from the Mall. Food is simple Indian and Chinese-style hill fare. For momos, thukpa and cheaper meals, the lanes around Chowk Bazaar and Laden La Road are a ten-minute walk downhill.

name: Tenzing Norgay Youth Hostel
price_band: ₹300–700 a dorm bed (indicative, check current tariff)
image_query: Youth Hostel Darjeeling Zakir Hussain Road
summary: A government youth hostel on Dr Zakir Hussain Road, high above the Mall, with a 44-bed dormitory and a handful of rooms. Basic, cheap and well placed for students and backpackers, with some of the best free mountain views in town. Managed under the GTA.
body: The youth hostel is a large three-storey building on Dr Zakir Hussain Road, the ridge-top lane that has drawn backpackers to Darjeeling for decades. It is about a quarter of an hour on foot from the Mall, mostly uphill, and that height is the point: on clear mornings the Kanchenjunga range sits across the window. It is named after Tenzing Norgay, who made Darjeeling his home. Tenzing lived in the town for decades and trained climbers at the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute from 1954.

It is built for students and low-budget travellers: a 44-bed dormitory, two double rooms and one larger room, with shared bathrooms and no frills. Families wanting private rooms will do better elsewhere. Bring a sleeping-bag liner and a warm layer in winter. The hostel is managed under the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration, and booking rules, membership requirements and tariffs can change, so check current status before you travel. Cheap cafés and small lodges line the same lane.
why: Among the cheapest beds in Darjeeling
Ridge-top position with mountain views on clear days
Surrounded by the budget cafés and lodges of Zakir Hussain Road

faqs.q: Does the Darjeeling youth hostel have private rooms?
faqs.a: Only a few. The Tenzing Norgay Youth Hostel is mainly a 44-bed dormitory, with two double rooms and one larger room. It suits students, school groups and solo backpackers. Couples and families who want privacy should book early for the doubles or choose a budget hotel near Clubside or a government lodge instead.

faqs.q: How far is the youth hostel from the Mall?
faqs.a: About 15 minutes on foot, mostly uphill along Dr Zakir Hussain Road. The climb is the price of the view: the hostel sits high on the ridge. Taxis can reach the road, but the lanes are narrow. Walking back after dinner in the dark is fine on the main lane; carry a torch.

faqs.q: Who runs the Tenzing Norgay Youth Hostel?
faqs.a: It is a government youth hostel, now managed under the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration (GTA). That means low fixed tariffs but also changing booking rules: at times beds have been bookable only in person or by phone. Check current status before you travel, and arrive early in the day in peak season.

name: Lowis Jubilee Complex
summary: A government tourist complex on Dr S. K. Pal Road, run under the GTA. Plain rooms at modest rates in a quieter part of town, a sensible choice for groups and families who want a government tariff and do not mind a walk to the Mall.
body: Lowis Jubilee Complex is one of the government tourist properties of the Darjeeling hills, on Dr S. K. Pal Road. It is the kind of place hill families and school groups have used for years: large, plain, and priced to government norms rather than to the view. Rooms are simple, linen is clean, and the setting is calmer than the hotels around Chowk Bazaar. It is also handy for the Lebong side of town and the road down towards Happy Valley tea garden.

Because it is not right on the Mall, you will walk more or take short taxi hops, so factor that in with older travellers. In return, rates tend to be lower than central private hotels in peak season. Ask about heating, hot water and meals when you book. Tariffs and booking methods for GTA properties change, so check current status before you travel. Groups should confirm the number of rooms and beds in writing a few days before arrival.
why: Government tariffs, useful in peak weeks
Quieter part of town than the market area
Suits groups and families booking several rooms

faqs.q: Where is Lowis Jubilee Complex in Darjeeling?
faqs.a: On Dr S. K. Pal Road, away from the busiest part of the market. It is a walk or a short taxi ride from Chowrasta and the Mall, depending on your pace. The calmer position suits groups and families, but older travellers should plan short taxi hops for the uphill stretches at the end of the day.

faqs.q: Who manages Lowis Jubilee Complex?
faqs.a: It is a government tourist property now managed under the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration (GTA), along with lodges such as Maple Tourist Lodge and Jorepokhri Tourist Lodge. Booking is usually by phone or through the GTA tourism office in Darjeeling. Methods change from year to year, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Lowis Jubilee Complex good for a school or college group?
faqs.a: It is one of the better fits in town. Government complexes like this have more rooms of a plain, practical kind and modest fixed tariffs, which makes a group booking simpler than splitting across private hotels. Book well ahead for October and the summer holidays, and confirm meals in advance.

name: Maple Tourist Lodge
summary: A GTA tourist lodge on Eric Benjamin Road in the Old Kutchery area of Darjeeling. Simple government rooms, an older building, and a quieter location than the market lanes. Good value for travellers who want a fixed government tariff in town.
body: Maple Tourist Lodge is one of the smaller government lodges in Darjeeling, on Eric Benjamin Road near the old court (Kutchery) area. It is a plain, older property: high ceilings, simple furniture and the sort of creaking wooden floors common in the town's colonial-era buildings. Rooms are priced to government norms. The Kutchery area grew up around the district courts and offices of British Darjeeling, and much of that era's building stock survives nearby, which makes for an interesting walk up to the ridge in the morning.

It works best for travellers who value a quiet night and a known tariff over a Mall-side address. You will walk uphill to Chowrasta or take a short taxi. Ask about room heaters in winter and whether meals are served on the day you arrive. Like other GTA properties, tariffs and booking channels change, so check current status before you travel. Rates are usually lower in the monsoon and winter months.
why: Fixed government tariff
Quieter area near the old court buildings
Older hill building with character

faqs.q: How do I book Maple Tourist Lodge in Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Usually by phone or through the GTA tourism office in Darjeeling, as Maple Tourist Lodge is run under the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration. Online booking for GTA lodges has come and gone over the years. Call ahead, confirm the tariff and meals, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Maple Tourist Lodge close to the Mall?
faqs.a: It is a walk, not a step. The lodge is on Eric Benjamin Road in the Old Kutchery area, below and to the side of the main ridge. Fit travellers walk up to Chowrasta in about 15 to 20 minutes; others take a short taxi. The trade-off is a quieter street at night.

faqs.q: Is Maple Tourist Lodge suitable in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, with preparation. Like most older hill buildings it is cold from December to February, when Darjeeling nights fall to about 2 °C. Ask for a heater and extra blankets, confirm hot-water timings, and bring warm layers for the evenings. Winter rates are often lower, and the mountain views are at their clearest.

name: Jorepokhri Tourist Lodge
summary: A GTA tourist lodge beside the twin ponds of Jorepokhri, near Sukhia Pokhari, about 20 km from Darjeeling at roughly 2,250 m. Cold, quiet and forested, with simple rooms and very little to do but walk, read and watch the mist come in.
body: The lodge stands by the two small ponds that give Jorepokhri its name, inside India's first salamander sanctuary, declared in 1985. It is a simple government building at altitude: rooms are basic, nights are cold for much of the year, and the forest of cryptomeria and oak around it is often wrapped in cloud by afternoon. Mornings in October, November and spring can be clear enough to see the Kanchenjunga range.

Come for silence, not facilities. Sukhia Pokhari's market is about 4 km away for supplies and onward jeeps to Mirik or Maneybhanjan. Meals are basic and should be arranged in advance. GTA tariffs and booking methods change, so check current status before you travel. Bring a torch, warm layers and something to read: evenings here are long, quiet and dark, with very little traffic on the road after sunset. Mim tea garden and the Simana viewpoint above Nepal are both short drives away for a morning outing.
why: One of very few places to sleep right by the twin ponds
Government tariff in a forest setting
Easy base for Sukhia Pokhari, Simana and Lepchajagat

faqs.q: Can I see salamanders at Jorepokhri?
faqs.a: Probably not. Jorepokhri was declared India's first salamander sanctuary in 1985, but recent reporting (2026) says paving and tourist building around the ponds altered the habitat so much that the Himalayan salamander is no longer found breeding there. Come for the forest and the quiet, and do not disturb the water's edge.

faqs.q: How cold is Jorepokhri Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Cold. At about 2,250 m it is a little higher than Darjeeling, and winter nights can fall below freezing. Even in May evenings are chilly. Ask for heaters and extra blankets, confirm hot water, and pack a down jacket or thick fleece from October to April.

faqs.q: How do I get to Jorepokhri Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Take a shared jeep from Darjeeling towards Sukhia Pokhari (about ₹70–100 a seat), then a local taxi for the last 4 km, or hire a car from Darjeeling for about ₹1,500–2,000 one way. The road runs via Ghoom and Lepchajagat. Check current status before you travel, especially in the monsoon.

name: WBFDC Lepchajagat Nature & Wilderness Resort
summary: A small forest property of the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation at Lepchajagat, about 2,120 m. A two-storey building with six rooms in pine, oak and rhododendron forest; two upper rooms have balconies facing the mountains. Booked online on the WBFDC portal.
body: The WBFDC lodge at Lepchajagat is one of the forest corporation's eco-tourism stays, set among tall trees about 19 km from Darjeeling on the road to Sukhia Pokhari and Mirik. It is small, which keeps it quiet: six rooms in a two-storey building, with the two first-floor rooms having private balconies that look towards the snow peaks on clear mornings. The forest corporation chose the site for its trees and its silence, and there is no town around it, only a few village houses and a small tea shop or two by the road.

Bookings open 90 days before the date of stay on the WBFDC online portal, and the balcony rooms go first for October–November and spring weekends. The day here is simple: dawn at the village viewpoint, birds in the forest, a walk to Ghoom or Sukhia, and an early dinner because the evenings are cold. Tariffs and booking rules change, so check current status before you travel.
why: Only six rooms, so it stays quiet
Forest setting at about 2,120 m with mountain views on clear days
Bookable online 90 days ahead on the WBFDC portal

faqs.q: How do I book the WBFDC resort at Lepchajagat?
faqs.a: Online, through the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation booking portal. Bookings open 90 days before the date of stay. The two first-floor rooms with balconies are the most asked for, so book on the day booking opens for October, November and long weekends. Check current status before you travel, as tariffs change.

faqs.q: Is there anything to do at Lepchajagat?
faqs.a: Very little, which is the point. You watch the dawn on Kanchenjunga from the village viewpoint, walk the forest roads for birds, and visit Ghoom or Sukhia Pokhari by shared jeep. Mist rolls in most afternoons, so plan views early. Families who want activities all day should stay in Darjeeling and visit for a morning.

faqs.q: How far is Lepchajagat from Darjeeling?
faqs.a: About 19 km, roughly 45 minutes to an hour by road via Ghoom on the road to Sukhia Pokhari and Mirik. A reserved car costs about ₹1,200–1,800 one way, or you can take a shared jeep towards Sukhia Pokhari and get off at Lepchajagat. Check current status before you travel in the monsoon.
